teaser: Agents need direction: every skill in one role, contained by scope, steered by people, and teams that send each other pull requests.
core_idea: Agents can go in all directions and bring every skill to a focused role, so they must be contained by scope and repository boundaries and steered by people who sometimes slow things down; and because they can do the work themselves, teams of agents should send each other pull requests that villagers and town planners later refactor or replace.

nodes.label: Agents need direction
nodes.summary: They can go in all directions.

nodes.label: Pull requests between teams
nodes.summary: Explorer code handed to the owner.

quotes.text: A human team would need five people for that.

figures.caption: One role, many skills, one scope: the historian at the centre, and around it the data scientist, the designer, the developer and the architect that the same agent can also be; around all of them, the scope that contains it, writing only its own paths, appending in its own rows, and asking the editor for anything else; outside, another team's code, pages and data, where it asks or sends a change.

Teams that send each other pull requests: an agent needs a feature another team owns; it builds the smallest thing that works, as an explorer, in its own space; it sends it to the owning team as a pull request, which that team reviews and decides; the villagers refactor it to the team's guidelines, with a human; and the town planner replaces it with shared code when the pattern is clear. Below, the humans give the direction.
